name: Lateral Ankle Sprain Rehabilitation Protocol
description: Evidence-based 4-phase program for lateral ankle sprain. From protection and decongestion (PEACE & LOVE) through early mobilization and proprioception to return to sport and recurrence prevention.
pain_rule: Max. 3/10 pain during exercise. Mild swelling after training is acceptable if it resolves within 24h. Sharp or increasing pain requires a break.
evidence_base: Dubois & Esculier (2019): PEACE & LOVE Protocol. BJSM
Verhagen et al. (2004): Neuromuscular training reduces recurrence rate ~50%. Cochrane
van den Bekerom et al. (2012): Early functional treatment > immobilization
progression_criteria: Pain level acceptable (max. 3/10 during exercise, resolves within 24h)
Swelling has reduced compared to the previous week
Sets/reps completed in 2 consecutive training sessions
No increase in instability feeling or tendency to roll over

phase_education.1:
**Phase 1: Protection & Decongestion (Week 0-1)**

In this phase, we follow the PEACE & LOVE protocol. Protection from loading, elevation, compression, and education in the acute phase — followed by early loading, circulation promotion, and pain-free mobility.

**Goal:** Swelling reduction, pain-free ROM, maintain muscle activation.

**Strategy:**
- Ankle pumps and alphabet tracing for active decongestion
- Isometric peroneal activation without ligament loading
- Seated stretches without weight-bearing
- Proximal activation (hip) for overall stability

**Scientific basis:** The PEACE & LOVE protocol replaces classic RICE. Early active movement promotes healing without overloading the injured structures (Dubois & Esculier 2019).
phase_education.2:
**Phase 2: Early Mobilization & ROM (Week 1-3)**

The acute swelling is receding. Now we begin with active mobilization and early weight-bearing.

**Goal:** Active mobility, early loading, bilateral strengthening.

**Strategy:**
- Active ROM in all planes
- Bilateral heel raises and seated calf raises
- Resistance band eversion and dorsiflexion
- Assisted single-leg stance for initial proprioception stimuli
- Gait training on level ground

**Scientific basis:** Early functional treatment is superior to immobilization — faster return to activities with equal or better stability (van den Bekerom et al. 2012).
phase_education.3:
**Phase 3: Strengthening & Proprioception (Week 3-8)**

Focus on strengthening the peroneal muscles and progressive neuromuscular training — the two most important protective factors against recurrence.

**Goal:** Peroneal muscles, neuromuscular training, progressive balance.

**Strategy:**
- Peroneal strengthening with increasing resistance
- Single-leg stance progressive (eyes open > closed > unstable surface)
- Balance pad / wobble board for reflexive stabilization
- Lateral band walks, sagittal and lateral lunges
- Tandem walk and eccentric stair descent

**Scientific basis:** Neuromuscular training reduces recurrence rate by ~50% through improvement of reflexive peroneal activation (Verhagen et al. 2004).
phase_education.4:
**Phase 4: Return to Sport & Prevention (Week 8-12+)**

You are ready for sport-specific loading. The goal is complete return and a long-term prevention program.

**Goal:** Sport-specific loading, recurrence prevention.

**Strategy:**
- Single-leg hops in various directions
- Jump rope bilateral > unilateral
- T-test agility drills for rapid direction changes
- Sport-specific cutting movements
- Maintenance program 2x/week long-term

**Scientific basis:** Stepwise return to sport (50% > 75% > 100% over 3-4 weeks) with criteria: pain-free, full ROM, strength (single-leg heel raise 25x), balance (30s single-leg stance eyes closed).

exercises.name: Ankle Pumps (Dorsiflexion/Plantarflexion)
exercises.description: Seated, slowly move the foot up and down (dorsiflexion/plantarflexion). Pain-free range of motion. Promotes circulation and reduces swelling.
exercises.phase_goal: Swelling reduction, pain-free mobility

exercises.name: Alphabet Tracing with the Foot
exercises.description: Seated, trace the entire alphabet in the air with your foot. Promotes active mobility in all planes without loading.
exercises.phase_goal: Swelling reduction, pain-free mobility

exercises.name: Toe Curls (Towel Exercise)
exercises.description: Seated, grip and scrunch a towel with your toes. Strengthens intrinsic foot muscles and improves proprioception.
exercises.phase_goal: Swelling reduction, pain-free mobility

exercises.name: Isometric Eversion
exercises.description: Press the foot outward against a wall or solid object. Submaximal, no pain. Maintains peroneal activation without loading the ligament.
exercises.phase_goal: Swelling reduction, pain-free mobility

exercises.name: Isometric Inversion
exercises.description: Press the foot inward against a wall or solid object. Submaximal, no pain. Maintains muscle activation.
exercises.phase_goal: Swelling reduction, pain-free mobility

exercises.name: Hip Abduction (Side-Lying)
exercises.description: Lying on your side, raise the upper leg. Keeps proximal muscles active while the ankle is protected.
exercises.phase_goal: Swelling reduction, pain-free mobility

exercises.name: Calf Stretch (Seated, Passive)
exercises.description: Seated, perform a gentle calf stretch using a towel or band around the ball of the foot. No pain in the ankle.
exercises.phase_goal: Swelling reduction, pain-free mobility

exercises.name: Bilateral Squats (Unloaded)
exercises.description: Bilateral squats while holding onto a stable object. ROM maintenance in the lower extremity without overloading the ankle.
exercises.phase_goal: Swelling reduction, pain-free mobility

exercises.name: Active ROM All Planes
exercises.description: Active movement of the ankle in all planes: dorsiflexion, plantarflexion, eversion, inversion. Full pain-free range of motion.
exercises.phase_goal: Active mobility, early loading, bilateral strengthening

exercises.name: Bilateral Heel Raises
exercises.description: Rise onto tiptoes on both feet and lower in a controlled manner. Building calf muscles and early ankle loading.
exercises.phase_goal: Active mobility, early loading, bilateral strengthening

exercises.name: Band Eversion (Light)
exercises.description: Using a light resistance band, move the foot outward (eversion) against the resistance. Building the peroneal muscles.
exercises.phase_goal: Active mobility, early loading, bilateral strengthening

exercises.name: Band Dorsiflexion
exercises.description: Using a resistance band, pull the foot upward (dorsiflexion) against the resistance. Strengthens the tibialis anterior.
exercises.phase_goal: Active mobility, early loading, bilateral strengthening

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance (Assisted)
exercises.description: Stand on one leg with light fingertip support on a wall. Basic proprioception training.
exercises.phase_goal: Active mobility, early loading, bilateral strengthening

exercises.name: Single-Leg Squats (Assisted)
exercises.description: Single-leg squats while holding onto a stable object. Focus on leg axis stability and controlled movement.
exercises.phase_goal: Active mobility, early loading, bilateral strengthening

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raises (Bilateral)
exercises.description: Seated, raise the heels. Strengthens the soleus muscle. Bilateral as a precursor to single-leg training.
exercises.phase_goal: Active mobility, early loading, bilateral strengthening

exercises.name: Gait Training (Level Ground)
exercises.description: Conscious walking on level ground with correct gait pattern. Practice heel-strike, midstance, toe-off.
exercises.phase_goal: Active mobility, early loading, bilateral strengthening

exercises.name: Peroneal Strengthening with Band
exercises.description: Using a medium to heavy resistance band, press the foot outward (eversion) against the resistance. Target muscle: peroneal muscles.
exercises.phase_goal: Peroneal muscles, neuromuscular training, progressive balance

exercises.name: Tibialis Anterior Strengthening
exercises.description: Using a resistance band, pull the foot forcefully upward (dorsiflexion) against the resistance. Strengthens the anterior lower leg muscles.
exercises.phase_goal: Peroneal muscles, neuromuscular training, progressive balance

exercises.name: Single-Leg Heel Raise
exercises.description: Standing on one leg, raise the heel and lower in a controlled manner. Progressive calf loading and balance training.
exercises.phase_goal: Peroneal muscles, neuromuscular training, progressive balance

exercises.name: Single-Leg Stance (Eyes Open > Closed)
exercises.description: Stand on one leg: first with eyes open (30s), then with eyes closed (20s). Progressive proprioception challenge.
exercises.phase_goal: Peroneal muscles, neuromuscular training, progressive balance

exercises.name: Balance Pad / Wobble Board
exercises.description: Standing on an unstable surface (balance pad or wobble board). First bilateral, then single-leg. Challenges reflexive ankle stabilization.
exercises.phase_goal: Peroneal muscles, neuromuscular training, progressive balance

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walks
exercises.description: With a resistance band around the ankles, perform controlled side steps. Strengthens gluteal muscles and the lateral chain.
exercises.phase_goal: Peroneal muscles, neuromuscular training, progressive balance

exercises.name: Sagittal Lunges
exercises.description: Forward and backward lunges. Controlled leg axis, knee over toes. Functional strengthening.
exercises.phase_goal: Peroneal muscles, neuromuscular training, progressive balance

exercises.name: Lateral Lunges
exercises.description: Side lunges. Trains lateral stability and challenges ankle control in the frontal plane.
exercises.phase_goal: Peroneal muscles, neuromuscular training, progressive balance

exercises.name: Tandem Walk
exercises.description: Walking in a line, heel to toe. Tests and trains dynamic balance.
exercises.phase_goal: Peroneal muscles, neuromuscular training, progressive balance

exercises.name: Eccentric Stair Descent
exercises.description: Descending stairs with controlled eccentrics. Loads the calf muscles eccentrically and challenges ankle control.
exercises.phase_goal: Peroneal muscles, neuromuscular training, progressive balance

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hop (Anterior/Lateral/Medial)
exercises.description: Single-leg jumps in various directions (forward, sideways, diagonal). Tests reactive stability and confidence.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-specific loading, recurrence prevention

exercises.name: Jump Rope (Bilateral > Single-Leg)
exercises.description: Jump rope: first bilateral, then single-leg. Plyometric training and ankle conditioning.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-specific loading, recurrence prevention

exercises.name: Change of Direction Drills (T-Test)
exercises.description: T-test agility drill: sprint forward, side shuffles left/right, sprint back. Trains rapid direction changes.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-specific loading, recurrence prevention

exercises.name: Cutting Movements
exercises.description: Rapid direction changes with abrupt stopping and change of direction. Simulating sport-specific loading.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-specific loading, recurrence prevention

exercises.name: Sport-Specific Agility
exercises.description: Sport-specific movement patterns with progressive speed and complexity. Adapted to the demands of your sport.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-specific loading, recurrence prevention

exercises.name: Prevention Maintenance Program
exercises.description: Maintenance program for recurrence prevention: combination of proprioception, strengthening, and neuromuscular training. Continue 2x/week long-term.
exercises.phase_goal: Sport-specific loading, recurrence prevention
